recommended.rule: Rent or value for a county: (1) the ACS 2020-2024 published county median; (2) where Census withholds it, blend in inverse variance (log scale, bias corrected) the county's own latest published ACS 5-year median from the 2018-2023 vintages (only a vintage with 30 or more renter or owner households), rolled forward by its state's household-weighted median change, and the median of the smaller half of adjacent counties (Census adjacency file) that publish one; (3) Kalawao's value: pooled East and West Molokai CCD median; (4) the state weighted median only if nothing else exists.
recommended.validationOnSmallCounties: Rolled-forward own history misses the published median by a median 4 to 5 percent (90th percentile 14 to 16 percent) one vintage back; adjacent-county medians (smaller half) by 11 to 20 percent; the old state-weighted figure by 40 to 70 percent and always too high.

unit: dollars (monthly gross rent; median home value)
basis: ACS 2020-2024 5-year (api.census.gov, key used, key not stored) withholds one or both medians for 10 of 3,222 counties: Alpine and Sierra CA (rent), Kalawao HI (value), Borden, King and Terrell TX (rent), Crockett and Edwards TX (value), Kenedy and Loving TX (both). The stopgap named Culberson TX, which publishes both. Interpolating the ACS bin counts reproduces published medians within 0.1 percent, so withheld ones are suppressed estimates, not missing tables. I tested replacement rules on the 327 (value) and 1,104 (rent) small counties that do publish: own history rolled forward by state change is far closer than neighbor medians and about ten times closer than the old state-weighted mean (which overstates small rural counties by about 70 percent in value). The recommended values blend the two by their measured error variances; ranges are the 10th to 90th percentile of that blend's error. Crockett's own 2024 bins say $69,419 but its 2023 median was $140,000, so the 2024 bins are not used. Kalawao has no owner-occupied homes in any vintage, so the Molokai pool stands in. Island Areas medians come from the 2020 Census (not ACS), as reported in 2020 dollars.

recommended.cohabitationLead: ESTIMATE, not Census: 80 percent of 2020-2022 first marriages were preceded by cohabitation (NCFMR/NSFG); earlier cohorts were lower but no fetched page gives their shares; the length of that cohabitation is not in any fetched source, so keep 2 years times the cohort's cohabiting share (low 1 year, high 3).

basis: Marriage age comes straight from Census: CPS Table MS-2 (period medians 1890 to 2025, turned into cohort medians by finding the age a at which the period median in year b+a equals a) and ACS 2020-2024 B12007 for every state, DC and Puerto Rico (men 30.6, women 28.7 nationally). The gap from marriage to first birth is an ACS PUMS 2022-2024 measurement on 23,755 women (2.46 million weighted) who gave birth in the last 12 months, are married once and have one child at home; it rises with the mother's age (1.5 years at 20-24 to 6.5 at 40+). Weaknesses: marriage dates only (cohabitation start is not in any Census table), ACS age distribution of first mothers runs older than birth certificates (median 30), a retrospective check on first-marriage couples with children at home gives a median of 1.5 to 2.5 years but is biased low for young wives and high for older ones, and earlier cohorts are not observed (assumed to follow the same age-at-birth gap). Island Areas first-marriage ages are singulate-mean-age equivalents calibrated on the 50 states and DC (correlation 0.96, residual SD 0.4 years).

recommended.placeScaling: Share of an adult's parents beyond an hour = 0.35 times the place's in-migrant index, (1 minus the share of 25-54 residents born in the state) over the national 0.501 (ACS B06001). Share of a parent's adult children beyond an hour = 0.28 times the place's out-migration index, (its interstate departure rate of 18-34 year olds, B07401) over the national 0.0467, held to 0.5-2. Both clamped 0.05 to 0.85.
recommended.hourToCounty: A person leaving the county is still within an hour about 38 percent of the time nationally (ACS county-to-county flows 2016-2020: adjacent county or within 50 miles), so county-outside share = beyond-an-hour share / (1 minus that share); for the national anchors that is 0.57 of parents and 0.45 of adult children outside the county, not 0.35 and 0.28.

basis: The national levels are Pew survey figures, not Census. The scaling by an index is a modeling choice, not a Census statistic, so the place variation is low confidence; the national anchors are medium. ACS 5-year B07401 gives within-county moves and county-leaving moves by age and state for the scale ceiling. incomeTaxRateOrStructureChangedJan2025To.OK: six brackets -> three, top 4.75 -> 4.5 on Jan 1 2026 (HB2764)

incomeTaxRateOrStructureChangedJan2025To.WA: capital gains tax made graduated, new 9% over $1M (SB5813), retroactive Jan 1 2025

changedAfterStart.salesTaxStateRateChanged: none among 50 states and DC between Jan 2025 and Jul 2026 (only local and rounding changes); Louisiana 4.45 -> 5.0 took effect Jan 1 2025, before the start, so 5.0 is correct for the start
changedAfterStart.snap: all 48 states, DC, AK, HI, GU, VI changed Oct 1 2025 (FY2026 COLA); use FY2025 table above for Jan 20 2025
changedAfterStart.propertyTax: effective rates drift yearly (2023 and 2024 columns both given); no statutory state rate series to carry back

unit: per-series: percent rates; USD per month (SNAP); USD per week and weeks (UI); federal share fraction (FMAP)
basis: Values are the Tax Foundation tables dated January 1, 2025 (income and sales), USDA FNS FY2025 tables (SNAP), DOL OUI significant provisions effective January 2025 (UI), and KFF/Federal Register FY2025 FMAPs, all fetched this session. Income tax carries all single-filer brackets, so the game can replay a graduated schedule. Property tax is an effective rate on owner-occupied housing (ACS-based, 2023 column), not a statutory rate. The 2026 tables were also fetched and diffed so the changedAfterStart block lists exactly which places had enacted changes (several were retroactive to Jan 1 2025 but enacted after Jan 20 2025, so were not in force on the start date). Territory income, sales and property values, Guam UI, and AS/MP UI were not found in a fetched page and are low-confidence estimates.
